commit.message:
Add bounded model checking with Kani

The simulator picks message orderings at random. Kani, a model checker
for Rust, tries every ordering within a bound instead, on the library as
it is, with no changes to it.

The new verify crate holds a cluster driver and the harnesses. The
driver runs real replicas and clients, keeps every message and reply
ever sent in a list that delivery never removes, so any message can
arrive again, out of order, or never, and takes one caller-chosen step
at a time. After each step it asserts the simulator's safety properties.
The harnesses feed it symbolic choices, so Kani explores every sequence
of them: one request with any delivery, two clients interleaving, and a
one-period primary timeout so view changes fire with a request in
flight. Under a plain cargo build only the driver and its unit tests
compile.

The harness bounds are a first guess and no harness has yet run to
completion; the README says how to run them.

 is recorded in its commit message with the seed and the commit that
 reproduces it.
 
+### Model checking
+
+The simulator picks message orderings at random and hopes to hit the bad
+one. [`verify/`](verify) uses [Kani](https://model-checking.github.io/kani/),
+a model checker for Rust, to try every ordering instead. A harness builds a
+cluster of real replicas and clients, and then takes a fixed number of
+steps where every choice is symbolic: which message to deliver, out of
+order or again, which replica to tick, which client to send. Kani explores
+every sequence of those choices and checks the simulator's safety
+properties after each step, so within a harness's bounds the result is
+exhaustive. Beyond them it says nothing, and the bounds are small: three
+replicas, a handful of steps, one or two view changes. Long enough for a
+request to commit and a view change to complete, short enough for the
+solver to finish.
+
+Kani is a separate install:
+
+```console
+cargo install --locked kani-verifier
+cargo kani setup
+```
+
+Then run every harness, or one by name:
+
+```console
+cargo kani -p vsr-verify
+cargo kani -p vsr-verify --harness view_change_with_request_in_flight
+```
+
+The harnesses are in [`verify/harnesses.rs`](verify/harnesses.rs). Each
+one names its bounds. Expect minutes rather than seconds per harness, because
+every hash map lookup in the replica is a formula for the solver. A failing
+harness prints the assertion that failed and, with `--concrete-playback`,
+generates a unit test that replays the sequence of choices that reached it.
+
 ## References
 
 1. Barbara Liskov and James Cowling. [Viewstamped Replication Revisited](https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/80846d94-fcd3-40e6-87fb-8d91fe99a5d1). MIT-CSAIL-TR-2012-021, 2012. The protocol this library implements.

+//! Bounded model checking of vsr-rs with Kani.
+//!
+//! [`cluster`] drives a small cluster of real replicas and clients. The
+//! caller chooses every step: which message to deliver, which replica to
+//! tick, which client to make a request. After each step the cluster
+//! asserts the same properties the simulator checks. The harnesses in
+//! `harnesses` feed it symbolic choices, so `cargo kani` explores every
+//! delivery order, loss, replay, and view change within the harness bounds.
+//!
+//! Run with `cargo kani -p vsr-verify`, or a single harness with
+//! `cargo kani -p vsr-verify --harness <name>`. Under a plain `cargo build`
+//! only the cluster driver and its unit tests compile.
+
+// Kani's `assert!` takes its message as a plain literal, without
+// interpolation, so the variables named in the messages count as unused
+// under Kani only.
+#![cfg_attr(kani, allow(unused_variables))]
+
+pub mod cluster;
+
+#[cfg(kani)]
+mod harnesses;
